title: Direct guest harness runtime and guest workload control
objective: Install and run the model-agnostic Little Mester harness directly inside the outer VM guest, with native guest auth and broad guest-level control. Docker/Compose are available to the agent for arbitrary project workloads; no Docker container wraps the agent. Preserve the outer VM host-isolation boundary and existing restricted egress/secret rules.

acceptance_criteria.text: A selected harness (initially OpenCode) is installed and launched as a native guest process in the VM, not as a Docker container; it opens the TUI in the invoking session and operates on the selected workspace.

The guest agent can use Docker CLI and Compose against the guest daemon to start, inspect, stop and remove a representative project service (including PostgreSQL) and run tests in a repeated feedback loop.

Guest authority is documented accurately: the agent can administer its guest and guest Docker; this is not treated as host isolation. No host Docker socket, host filesystem outside the selected workspace, host credentials, or LAN access is exposed.

Guest Docker/Compose supports ordinary project workflows without a restrictive generated wrapper silently rewriting compose files or blocking normal guest-local service ports; guest workloads remain inside the outer VM boundary.

Nested VM support is explicitly tested: report host KVM nested VMX/SVM capability, guest CPU virtualization flags and /dev/kvm availability, then boot and stop a nested test VM. Unsupported hosts report a clear limitation; no nested support is claimed without a live pass.

Existing harness checks that apply to direct guest execution (verify-lab, TUI exit-confirm, metrics/model connectivity where configured) pass, and the same runner interface can select another supported harness without changing the VM trust boundary.
OpenCode version selection/update is reproducible and updates guest software without destroying the VM overlay or workspace; credential state is preserved or exported/imported through the #45 flow.

OpenCode running directly in the guest can call each configured local model provider (Ollama and llama.cpp) through an explicit, narrow VM-to-host API path and receive a valid completion response; the request succeeds in the TUI without Malformed_HTTP_Response, and no general host route or LAN exposure is added.

The direct guest TUI loads and displays the host metrics UI and exposes the host-metrics tool through an explicitly configured, narrow VM-safe path; missing service or transport failure is reported clearly rather than silently losing the feature.

The direct guest OpenCode TUI loads the Little Mester exit-confirm plugin: Ctrl-C opens the confirmation flow, cancel remains in the TUI, and confirm exits; record OpenCode version and actual observed behavior.

VM metrics are implemented and acceptance-tested as a VM-specific path without removing or regressing the existing host-Docker metrics path; the guest does not depend on Compose DNS or general host access, and transition/removal requires owner approval after both paths pass.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 2026-10-29 implementation adds a host-native curated metrics endpoint bound to 127.0.0.1:19532, independent of the existing Docker metrics service, and guestfwd remains limited to that endpoint. Local endpoint, host-service lifecycle, guest URL configuration, Bats and Python tests pass. Direct guest/TUI metrics acceptance remains unverified because this environment has no /dev/kvm or Docker. Owner CachyOS host check 2026-10-29: `./lab-vm metrics up` started endpoint on 127.0.0.1:19532; `metrics status` returned live CPU/RAM/NVIDIA GPU/temperature data. Subsequent `./lab-vm status` showed outer VM stopped, so guestfwd/TUI are not yet tested. Owner CachyOS live guest check 2026-10-29: after non-clean `./lab-vm up --debug --unsafe-recurse --auto-accept`, guest `curl -fsS` requests to `http://10.0.2.100:19532/summary`, `/metrics`, and `/history?n=5` all succeeded. Returned host CPU/RAM, NVIDIA GPU, temperatures, and rolling history via QEMU guestfwd. OpenCode TUI/tool rendering and LAN-negative check remain pending.

acceptance_criteria.text: Fresh VM guests install the latest OpenCode CLI by default; an explicit VM_OPENCODE_VERSION semantic-version pin remains supported. Ordinary `up` preserves an already installed version unless an explicit pin is selected; latest upgrades are deliberate via the update command.

`./lab-vm update` checks available updates and asks for confirmation before applying changes. With no target it checks/updates OpenCode, installed managed test tools, and the Little Mester guest config/plugins; individual targets can be selected, while `--all` additionally upgrades managed guest OS packages and the guest Docker Engine. `--yes` is the explicit non-interactive confirmation override.
Guest updates happen in place without deleting/recreating the VM overlay, base image, selected workspace, or credential state; normal agent launches do not download or install updates.

The focused metrics suite passes 7/7 and the complete VM Python suite passes 47/47. The owner-reported live guest reset is not yet retested; no live metrics/TUI acceptance is claimed.

2026-10-30 clarification: metrics are optional to OpenCode launch. `vm_cmd_agent` starts the host service and attempts a bounded guestfwd preflight; if startup or forwarding fails, it warns but continues, while the TUI shows transport failure and retries with bounded, non-overlapping requests. This preserves the documented core-agent behavior while making metrics failures explicit. Live CachyOS metrics reset still needs owner-host retest.

2026-10-30 local follow-up: fixed and independently syntax-checked the embedded preflight Python. Agent launch retains optional-metrics behavior: start the shared service and make a bounded 10s guestfwd readiness attempt; on failure, warn, disable this session's metrics URL, and still launch OpenCode. Local checks: complete VM Python suite 47/47, docs consistency 115/115, TUI JSX, Bash/Python syntax, and diff check pass; lab-vm self-tests 6 passed (QEMU/ISO unavailable in the self-test). No live guest/API/TUI retest or owner VM action was performed.

CORRECTION to the immediately preceding 2026-10-30 local follow-up: if host metrics service startup fails, the session gets a loopback-unavailable placeholder URL; if startup succeeds but the 10s guestfwd preflight fails, the session retains METRICS_URL=http://10.0.2.100:19532 so the TUI can report/retry that path. In both cases OpenCode launches. The embedded preflight Python syntax check and local suite results remain as recorded; no live guest retest was performed.

Local 2026-10-30: Bats 117/117, Python unittest 56/56, docs checks 115/115, CI ShellCheck commands, Bash syntax, diff check, and ticket validation pass. Update behavior is mock-tested only; no KVM/guest package update or host acceptance was performed.

Final local verification 2026-10-30 after latest-by-default and resolved-version install changes: Bats 117/117, Python unittest 57/57, docs 115/115, CI ShellCheck commands, Bash syntax, diff check, ticket validation all pass. No live VM/KVM package update was run.
Local 2026-10-30 focused model-path regression coverage added; no real model completion, guestfwd, or TUI acceptance claimed.

Local regression run after native endpoint and update-detection changes: Bats 123/123; VM Python unittest suite 63/63; `./lab-vm test` 8/8 after installing the same no-KVM CI prerequisites; cloud-init schema valid; CI ShellCheck commands, Ruff, Python compile, and docs consistency 115/115 pass. Node 20 package build/check and Jest 143/143 pass. Ticket-store validation passed before this ledger update. No KVM, guest model completion, or owner-host update was run.

Host model API path now accepts a healthy user-managed OpenAI-compatible server only when `ss` confirms the exact QEMU target is bound to 127.0.0.1; `models up/status` do not require Docker for that path. Unhealthy or wildcard listeners fail closed; optional Compose fallback remains. Real guest model completions/repeated streams and LAN-negative acceptance remain pending.

Guest update guard now checks the actual mester-owned OpenCode CLI process attached to a terminal rather than broad `pgrep -f`, ignores headless/no-TTY processes, and checks again immediately before applying any update. Mocked SSH and synthetic /proc regressions pass; live guest update acceptance remains pending.

Review follow-up found a fail-open mixed-publication edge: status previously accepted a mapping list when any entry was 127.0.0.1, despite an additional 0.0.0.0 entry. Added a regression first (it failed on the old implementation), then changed validation to require a non-empty list where every mapping is exactly 127.0.0.1:<expected-port>. Revalidated: Bats 123/123; VM Python 63/63; lab-vm self-tests 8/8; docs 115/115; ShellCheck, Ruff, Python compile, cloud-init schema and diff check pass. Node 20 package build/check/Jest 143/143 had passed before this shell-only follow-up. No KVM/owner-host model completion, repeated stream, live update, or GitHub Actions run was performed; host acceptance remains pending under #41/#42.

Follow-up hardened the same model-boundary path: unavailable or failing `ss` is no longer treated as no listener. `models up` now refuses Compose fallback and `models status` refuses Docker fallback when listener inspection cannot be completed. Regressions were run red-first and now pass. Final local checks: Bats 125/125; VM Python unittest 63/63; `./lab-vm test` 8/8; docs 115/115; ShellCheck, Ruff, Python compile, cloud-init schema, and diff check pass. Node 20 build/package/Jest 143/143 passed before these shell-only changes. No live owner-host/KVM/model-completion/update or GitHub Actions run; acceptance remains pending.

Further fail-closed review found Compose-config validation also accepted a list if any entry matched loopback. Added a mixed loopback+0.0.0.0 regression (red on the old validator); validation now requires every published mapping for the model service to be the exact expected loopback port. Final CI-equivalent local checks after all changes: Bats 125/125; VM Python 63/63; lab-vm self-tests 8/8; docs 115/115; ShellCheck, Ruff, Python compile, cloud-init schema, and git diff --check passed. Node 20 build/package/Jest 143/143 passed before these shell-only changes. No GitHub Actions run or owner-host/KVM acceptance was performed.

Compose-config follow-up: a second red-first test showed `_vm_validate_api_publish_config` accepted a resolved port list containing both 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 entries because it used `any()`. It now requires a non-empty list where every published model-service mapping is exactly the expected loopback target/port. Full local checks rerun after this fix: Bats 125/125, VM Python 63/63, lab-vm self-tests 8/8, docs 115/115, ShellCheck, Ruff, Python compile, cloud-init schema and diff check all pass. Node build/package/Jest 143/143 was already passing before shell-only changes. Owner host and GitHub Actions remain unrun.

Owner CachyOS report (2026-10-31): `./lab-vm egress-reload` succeeded; the one subsequent `./lab-vm models status` returned `llama.cpp API is listening on 127.0.0.1:8080 but its /health health check failed.` This is fail-closed and proves only that a loopback listener exists; it does not establish whether the listener is native or the Compose forwarder, nor backend/HTTP health. No VM agent/model completion was started. Next use read-only `./lab-vm models diagnose llamacpp` (initially without `-d`/`--sudo`) and return only redacted Docker version/context, resolved port mapping, sidecar/backend state and health, host listener, direct-container and loopback HTTP statuses. Do not recreate even the sidecar, start the agent, reload egress, change network/firewall, or alter backend/container state until those observations are reviewed. Do not paste any URLs, tokens, prompts, or sensitive log content.

Owner CachyOS read-only diagnosis (2026-10-31): egress-reload succeeded. Docker Engine 29.9.2; resolved Compose config has llamacpp-vm-api target/published 8080 on host_ip 127.0.0.1. Forwarder is running and both configured_bindings and runtime_ports show 127.0.0.1:8080; docker port agrees. The llama.cpp backend container is Exited (0), stopped about 41 hours earlier, and no running backend is present. Direct-container and host-loopback /health probes both timed out; host listener is loopback-only. The same-host non-loopback address probe did not connect, but this is not a separate-LAN isolation test. Docker journal logged attempts to delete nonexistent nftables tables; no causal link established. No repair/mutation was attempted. This localizes the immediate unhealthy endpoint to the stopped backend, not a missing Docker port mapping.

Diagnostic interpretation: the Docker forwarder has a correct runtime loopback binding but times out because its configured llama.cpp backend container has been stopped for ~41 hours. Host and direct-container /health both time out; model backend is not present/running. The local host IP probe is not remote-LAN proof. No container or VM state was changed. A supported `models down` → `models up llamacpp` recovery would start the Compose health-gated backend and may load GPU resources; await owner approval before running it.

Owner CachyOS report (2026-10-31): ran `./lab-vm models down` then `./lab-vm models up llamacpp`. This stopped only the API forwarder, then Compose started the stopped llama.cpp backend, waited for its healthy check, started the forwarder, and host `/health` passed. `./lab-vm models status` then reported healthy on 127.0.0.1:8080. This confirms the supported manual recovery sequence, but automatic recovery after host startup is still needed. Owner also reports direct guest model completions now work but OpenCode logs frequent `Retrying in 1s ... ECONNRESET: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly`; classify as partial/unusable, with cause and transport layer not yet isolated. No repeated-stream acceptance. Container startup was explicitly owner-run; no further service action taken by this agent.
